CustomerIdentifierItem.title: CustomerIdentifierItem
CustomerIdentifierItem.description:
A customer identifier.

A customer identifier is a unique identifier that is used to identify a customer. It can be an email address, a customer ID, a loyalty ID, a username, a browser ID, a device ID, a device fingerprint, or a hash of one of these identifiers. The type of the identifier is specified in the `type` field.

Where identiefiers exist in a global namespace, such as email addresses, the `system` should be set to `global`.
Where identifiers exist in a perishable, local namespace, such as browser IDs, the `system` should be set to `local`.
For owned and operated systems containing their own namespace, such as a CRM or Loyalty Program, the `system` should be set to the name of the system.

CustomerIdentifierType.title: CustomerIdentifierType
CustomerIdentifierType.description:
The type of the customer identifier. The enum values cover the following customer identifiers:
- `email` Email Address
- `emailhash_md5` MD5 Hash of Email Address
- `emailhash_sha1` SHA1 Hash of Email Address
- `emailhash_sha256` SHA256 Hash of Email Address
- `hash` Hash of an identifier
- `uuid` UUID (Universally Unique Identifier)
- `customer_id` Customer ID
- `crm_id` CRM ID
- `loyalty_id` Loyalty ID
- `username` Username (e.g. Twitter, Facebook or community forum username)
- `browser_id` Browser ID
- `device_id` Device ID
- `device_fingerprint` Device Fingerprint

Phone numbers and IP addresses are not included in this list because they are not considered reliable identifiers.

PageType.title: PageType
PageType.description:
The type of the page. The enum values cover the following page types:
- home (Homepage)
- category (Category Listing)
- search (Search Listing)
- details (Product Details Page)
- gallery (Gallery Page showing images of one or more products)
- article (Article Page with content)
- branded (Brand Store, Brand Search)
- cart (Cart Selection, Cart Review, Cart Confirmation)
- conversion (Order Confirmation, Order Complete)
- account (Login/Signup, Account Management, Wishlist/Favorites, Customer Support/Help, Shipping and Returns)
- about (About Us, Contact Us, Sitemap, Privacy Policy, Terms and Conditions, Reviews/Testimonials)

ProductIdentifierType.title: ProductIdentifierType
ProductIdentifierType.description:
The type of the product identifier. The enum values cover the following product identifiers:
- `product_id` Product ID: This is a unique identifier that a company assigns to its products. It's used internally to track products and is usually not visible to customers. The format and structure of a Product ID can vary widely from company to company. It could be numeric, alphanumeric, or a mix of both and often includes information about the product category, the manufacturer, and specific product details.
- `sku` SKU (Stock Keeping Unit): An SKU is a unique identifier that businesses use to track a specific item for inventory purposes. SKUs are often alphanumeric and can be designed to include a wide variety of information. For example, a retailer selling shoes might use an SKU that includes information about the style, color, and size of a pair of shoes. SKUs are company-specific. That means that each company has its own set of SKUs that are not shared or standardized across the industry.
- `upc` UPC (Universal Product Code): UPCs are standardized barcodes that are used across the entire retail industry. Each UPC is unique to the product it's attached to, and no two products share the same UPC. These barcodes are typically 12 digits long, with the first six to nine digits representing the company that manufactures or sells the product, and the remaining digits identifying the specific product and its attributes. The final digit is a check digit used to ensure the barcode has been entered (or scanned) correctly. The UPC system is managed by the GS1 organization, which ensures that each code is unique worldwide.
- `asin` ASIN (Amazon Standard Identification Numbers): This is a 10-character alphanumeric unique identifier that is assigned by Amazon to products that are sold through its platform.
- `ean` EAN (European Article Number): This is a barcode symbology that's primarily used in Europe for books, groceries, and other products.
- `isbn` ISBN (International Standard Book Number): This is an identifier that's used specifically for books.
- `mpn` MPN (Manufacturer Part Number): Used to identify a specific part of a product, typically used in manufacturing industries.
- `gtin` GTIN (Global Trade Item Number): This is a general term that encompasses UPC, EAN, and other barcode identifiers.
- `jan` JAN (Japanese Article Number): This is a barcode symbology that's primarily used in Japan.
- `nsn` NSN (National Stock Number): This is a 13-digit numeric code that identifies all the 'standardized material items of supply' as they have been recognized by all NATO countries.
- `plu` PLU (Price Look Up): This is used in supermarkets for fresh produce and bulk items, where UPCs are not feasible.
- `serial_number` Serial Number: A unique identifier assigned by the manufacturer.
- `model_number` Model Number: Identifier assigned by the manufacturer to indicate a product's design and features.
